concepts.name: Indentation-based block syntax
concepts.summary: Explain that consistent indentation, not braces, defines blocks and recognise an IndentationError.

concepts.name: Conditionals and loops
concepts.summary: Understand how if statements, for loops over iterables and while loops control the flow of a program.

concepts.name: Defining and calling functions
concepts.summary: Understand how def creates a function with parameters and a return value, and how calling it runs the body.

concepts.name: Running scripts and printing
concepts.summary: Recall how to run a .py file or the interactive interpreter and use print and input.

concepts.name: Variables and dynamic typing
concepts.summary: Understand that names are bound to objects of built-in types such as int, float, str and bool, and that types belong to values rather than names.

concepts.name: Lists and tuples
concepts.summary: Describe ordered sequences, indexing and slicing, and the difference between mutable lists and immutable tuples.

concepts.name: Dicts and sets
concepts.summary: Explain that dicts map unique keys to values and sets hold unique unordered items, and recall their literal syntax.

misconceptions.text: Indentation in Python is only for readability and can be changed freely without affecting behaviour.
A tuple can be changed in place just like a list.
A variable must be declared with a fixed type before it is used.

concepts.name: List comprehensions
concepts.summary: Write list, dict and set comprehensions with conditions to build collections from iterables.

concepts.name: Function arguments and defaults
concepts.summary: Use positional, keyword and default parameters plus *args and **kwargs when writing and calling functions.

concepts.name: Exception handling with try/except
concepts.summary: Catch specific exceptions with try/except/else/finally and raise errors deliberately.

concepts.name: Reading and writing files
concepts.summary: Open, read and write text files using the with statement so they are closed automatically.

concepts.name: Importing modules
concepts.summary: Import standard library modules and names and call their functions, and structure code across your own module files.

concepts.name: Basic standard library usage
concepts.summary: Use os and sys for paths and arguments, json to serialise data and datetime to handle dates.

concepts.name: Virtual environments and pip
concepts.summary: Create a venv, activate it and install third-party packages with pip.

concepts.name: String methods and formatting
concepts.summary: Use common string methods and f-strings to transform and format text.

misconceptions.text: A bare except clause is the best way to make code robust because it catches everything.
A default argument such as an empty list is created fresh on every call.
Files do not need to be closed because Python always writes data immediately.

concepts.name: Object identity and mutability
concepts.summary: Analyse how aliasing, shallow and deep copies, and mutable versus immutable objects affect program behaviour.

concepts.name: Classes and instances
concepts.summary: Define classes with attributes and methods and distinguish instance from class attributes.

concepts.name: Inheritance and special methods
concepts.summary: Analyse when to use inheritance with super() and implement dunder methods such as __repr__, __eq__ and __len__.

concepts.name: Generators and iterators
concepts.summary: Explain the iterator protocol and use yield and generator expressions to process data lazily.

concepts.name: Scope and closures
concepts.summary: Trace name resolution through local, enclosing, global and built-in scopes and explain how closures capture variables.

concepts.name: Decorators
concepts.summary: Analyse how a decorator wraps a function, and write one that preserves metadata with functools.wraps.

concepts.name: Collections module and containers
concepts.summary: Choose among defaultdict, Counter, deque and namedtuple for counting, grouping and queue tasks.

concepts.name: Packages and module layout
concepts.summary: Organise code into packages, understand how Python finds modules via sys.path, and use the main guard.

misconceptions.text: Assigning one list to another variable makes an independent copy.
A generator stores all its values in memory like a list.
Attributes defined at class level are always separate per instance.

concepts.name: Context managers
concepts.summary: Implement context managers via dunder methods or contextlib to guarantee resource cleanup and judge when to use them.

concepts.name: Dataclasses and typing hints
concepts.summary: Evaluate when annotations and dataclasses improve clarity and how static type checkers use them, given hints are not enforced at runtime.

concepts.name: Custom exception design
concepts.summary: Design exception hierarchies and use chaining to produce meaningful error handling across layers.

concepts.name: Descriptors and properties
concepts.summary: Analyse how properties and the descriptor protocol control attribute access and validation.

concepts.name: Concurrency models and the GIL
concepts.summary: Evaluate threads, processes and asyncio for I/O-bound versus CPU-bound work given the GIL.

concepts.name: Testing with pytest and unittest
concepts.summary: Write and structure unit tests with fixtures and mocks and analyse what they do and do not verify.

concepts.name: Profiling and performance tuning
concepts.summary: Measure with timeit and cProfile and judge optimisations by evidence rather than intuition.

concepts.name: Dependency and packaging management
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches to pinning dependencies and packaging a project for reproducible installs.

misconceptions.text: Python threads give true parallel speed-up for CPU-bound code.
Type hints are checked and enforced by the interpreter at runtime.
Optimising code without measuring is the quickest way to make it faster.

concepts.name: Metaclasses and class creation
concepts.summary: Design class-construction hooks using metaclasses, __init_subclass__ or class decorators and judge when simpler tools suffice.

concepts.name: Data model protocol design
concepts.summary: Create APIs that integrate with Python's data model through dunder methods, ABCs and structural protocols.

concepts.name: CPython memory and execution internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate how reference counting, cyclic garbage collection and bytecode execution affect behaviour and performance.

concepts.name: Advanced asynchronous architecture
concepts.summary: Design robust asynchronous systems with correct cancellation, backpressure and mixing of blocking code.

concepts.name: Extending Python with native code
concepts.summary: Evaluate options for native extensions against pure Python and decide when the integration cost is justified.

concepts.name: Library API and compatibility design
concepts.summary: Create stable, well-documented library interfaces with deliberate deprecation and compatibility strategies.

concepts.name: Import system customisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how finders, loaders and import hooks work and when customising imports is appropriate.

misconceptions.text: Metaclasses are the standard way to customise classes and should be used often.
Reference counting alone frees all unused objects, so garbage collection never matters.
Using async and await makes any code faster, including blocking or CPU-heavy code.
